Babcock & Wilcox.why: builds boiler + steam-turbine power plants for AI data centers (Base Electron project in North Dakota; 4-6 GW of new data-center power opportunities) - bookings and backlog surged on data-center power demand
Babcock & Wilcox.evidence: Babcock & Wilcox Q2 FY2026 (08-10-2026), CEO Kenny Young: our initial data center project with Base Electron is progressing ahead of expectations and on budget; manufacturing of the boilers, steam turbines and other long lead time components continues; B&W secured manufacturing reservation rights for an additional one gigawatt of steam turbines from Siemens Energy

players.product: boiler + steam-turbine power plants (coal / natural gas, enhanced combined cycle) for AI data-center campuses (Base Electron project, North Dakota)

quarterly_data.signal: Q2 2026 (CFO Cameron Frymyer): consolidated revenue $319.7 million, a 130% increase over Q2 2025; net income $14.3 million; adjusted EBITDA $21.8 million, up $7.9 million. First-half 2026 revenue $534.1 million versus $287.5 million, driven by large project volume including $131.7 million from Base Electron and the growing need for fossil-fuel electricity driven by AI, data centers and expanding economies.
quarterly_data.figure: revenue $319.7 million (+130% Y/Y); adjusted EBITDA $21.8 million; H1 Base Electron revenue $131.7 million

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Kenny Young raised the full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA target range 'from $80 million to $105 million' (as stated on the call), citing strong first-half results and visibility into continued strong demand in the second half.
quarterly_data.figure: 2026 adjusted EBITDA target $80 million to $105 million

quarterly_data.signal: Pipeline, bookings and backlog (CEO): total pipeline now over $14 billion, including 4-6 gigawatts of power generation opportunities added from hyperscalers, developers and utility customers; first-half 2026 bookings $2.7 billion, up more than 1,058% versus first-half 2025; backlog $2.6 billion at Q2 2026, up 533% year-over-year, fueled by core business growth and the Base Electron project in North Dakota.
quarterly_data.figure: pipeline >$14 billion (4-6 GW); H1 bookings $2.7 billion (+1,058%); backlog $2.6 billion (+533%)

quarterly_data.signal: Base Electron data-center power project (CEO): progressing ahead of expectations and on budget; manufacturing of boilers, steam turbines and other long-lead components continues; Base Electron has submitted its conditional use permit application, with most on-site construction (civil and mechanical) planned to start in the first part of 2027 and turbine and boiler components delivered after construction begins. B&W is in active discussions with multiple AI data center customers using coal and natural gas and expects a second data center project to move to full notice to proceed this year.
quarterly_data.figure: on-site construction from early 2027; second data-center project full notice to proceed expected in 2026

quarterly_data.signal: CEO on labor: availability of highly skilled labor, especially in the U.S., is in short supply; it hurt efficiencies and raised direct costs on a specific construction project in Q2. B&W is working with unions on incentives, rehires and delayed retirements and does not expect labor shortages to be persistent, as its construction focus has shifted toward variable price projects.

Technology and other projects (CEO): the BrightLoop commercial-scale demonstration at Massillon, Ohio is to begin site construction this fall, with the fuel reactor and hydrogen reactor initial phase operational by the latter part of 2027; B&W is working on the FEED study for the TerraSpark coal project and is in discussions on other coal-related projects for grid-connected or direct-connect data-center power. CEO: 'We don't see an end to the power generation demands coming from AI and data centers.'

players.product: gas turbines & grid technology for data-center power

connects_to.relationship: steam turbines for B&W boiler + steam-turbine data-center power plants

contracts.signal: B&W CEO Kenny Young: in anticipation of its next data center project, B&W secured the manufacturing reservation rights for an additional one gigawatt of steam turbines from Siemens Energy - a total of 20 50-megawatt steam turbines, with the first generator sets delivered within 12-14 months and further deliveries on a regular basis. The 50-megawatt boilers and steam turbines run in an enhanced combined cycle configuration that initially provides one gigawatt and can double to two gigawatts when combustion turbines are added later. CEO: B&W has a very close relationship with Siemens on supply chain and payment terms.
